title: Early severe skin disease with normal glucose
task: Audience: a clinician. Use 180–240 words in English. Give a one-sentence problem representation and explain why the presentation should not automatically be attributed to insulin resistance. Propose proportionate next genetic/systemic assessment and state what cannot yet be concluded. Do not predict a specific molecular result or diagnose an unreported systemic disorder. Give brief evidence-based justifications, not a private reasoning trace. Do not invent unreported findings, ages, test results or outcomes. Do not prescribe a dose or claim that an unreported result is normal.
opening: An eight-year-old boy had skin laxity at birth. From about age two, progressive hyperpigmented velvety thickening began in skin folds and became generalised. He has sparse curly hair, numerous skin tags, mild cognitive impairment, developmental delay, enamel erosion and low bone mineral density. No similar skin disorder is reported in the family.
initial_facts:
An eight-year-old boy had skin laxity at birth. From about age two, progressive hyperpigmented velvety thickening began in skin folds and became generalised. He has sparse curly hair, numerous skin tags, mild cognitive impairment, developmental delay, enamel erosion and low bone mineral density. No similar skin disorder is reported in the family.
Glucose status is described as normal. A popliteal skin biopsy shows hyperkeratosis, papillomatosis and acanthosis without an inflammatory infiltrate. Molecular results, chest imaging and treatment response have not been supplied.

scoring_condition: Evidence-only scoring of source-specific written tasks; inputs frozen before generation. D3a excludes provisional references and hidden outcomes.
reference: Integrate early-onset severe generalised skin findings with associated developmental and other features rather than treating normal glucose as proof that no relevant disease exists. A syndromic/genetic assessment and review for systemic involvement are defensible. Negative reported family history does not exclude a de novo disorder. Molecular cause, systemic investigation results and treatment response remain unknown. Keep the supplied individual separate from other patients.

criteria.name: Problem representation

anchors.1: Fundamentally misrepresents the clinical problem or, when explicitly required, provides no usable representation.
anchors.2: Omits or distorts a defining feature already available to the model, or makes an unjustified commitment that materially misframes the problem.
anchors.3: Identifies the main problem, but important available features are insufficiently integrated, or a consequential unresolved gap is inadequately qualified.
anchors.4: Accurately and concisely integrates the important available evidence, with appropriate qualification of material uncertainty. Minor limitations do not change the clinical framing.
anchors.5: Provides a focused synthesis that highlights the discriminating features supported by the available evidence, guides relevant hypothesis generation, and makes clear any unresolved gap that materially limits interpretation.

criteria.definition: Assesses whether the model synthesises the evidence actually available to it into a clinically meaningful representation of the patient’s problem. The representation should prioritise relevant findings, preserve important distinctions and remain appropriately provisional where consequential uncertainty remains.
criteria.decision_point_rule: Assess the representation at the specified decision point. Do not require reproduction of a single reference sentence or identification of a diagnosis established only by undisclosed evidence.
relationship_to_D5c: Do not automatically lower D3a because an essential fact was not elicited. Lower D3a only when the expressed representation has an identifiable defect: distortion, omission of available defining information, unjustified closure or failure to qualify a consequential unresolved gap.
Do not expect the model to name an undisclosed result. Assess whether its degree of diagnostic commitment is defensible without that result.
Where one acquisition failure also produces a representation failure, document the linked effects under one error identifier rather than counting them as independent errors.
criteria.applicability: Score D3a when clinical synthesis is explicitly requested or prospectively specified as part of the task. Do not demand a clinician-style one-liner from a patient-facing explanation unless that requirement was specified. Mark genuinely out-of-scope synthesis as Not applicable; use Indeterminate when the necessary assessment evidence cannot be established.

models.answer:
## Problem Representation

An eight-year-old boy with congenital skin laxity, progressive generalised acanthosis nigricans-like changes, sparse curly hair, skin tags, mild cognitive impairment, developmental delay, enamel erosion, and low bone mineral density, with normal glucose and a non-inflammatory papillomatous biopsy, presents a syndromic picture that extends beyond a simple insulin-resistance phenotype.

## Why Not to Attribute Automatically to Insulin Resistance

Acanthosis nigricans is classically associated with insulin resistance, but this association is not specific. In this case, normal glucose argues against a primary metabolic driver, and the constellation of congenital skin laxity, sparse curly hair, enamel erosion, low bone mineral density, and cognitive impairment points toward a broader connective-tissue or developmental syndrome rather than an isolated metabolic process. The biopsy showing hyperkeratosis, papillomatosis, and acanthosis without inflammatory infiltrate is morphologically consistent with acanthosis nigricans but does not distinguish a metabolic from a syndromic aetiology.

## Proportionate Next Steps

A targeted genetic evaluation, such as a chromosomal microarray or a gene panel encompassing connective-tissue and developmental genes, would be proportionate. Endocrine screening beyond glucose (insulin, IGF-1, thyroid function) and a formal developmental assessment are reasonable. Chest imaging and treatment response data are not yet available.

## What Cannot Yet Be Concluded

Without molecular results, imaging, or treatment response, a specific aetiology cannot be assigned. The presentation is syndromic but the underlying mechanism remains undetermined.

Attributing this presentation solely to insulin resistance is inappropriate because the patient has normal glucose status, which contradicts the typical metabolic profile of severe insulin resistance syndromes. Proportionate next steps include comprehensive genetic testing, such as whole-exome or whole-genome sequencing, to identify potential variants in genes associated with connective tissue disorders or developmental syndromes. Systemic assessment should focus on detailed dermatological mapping, ophthalmologic evaluation, and further metabolic profiling beyond glucose, including insulin levels and lipid panels, to clarify the endocrine status. Without molecular results, chest imaging, or treatment response data, a specific diagnosis cannot be confirmed. It remains unclear whether the skin findings are primary or secondary to an underlying genetic defect. The exact pathophysiology linking the skin laxity to the acanthosis nigricans is unknown. Additionally, the long-term prognosis and potential for systemic complications beyond the current findings cannot be predicted. Further investigation is required to distinguish between overlapping genetic syndromes and to determine if the normal glucose status is a transient finding or a stable characteristic of this specific condition.
